front.label: Front addition
front.title: A modern warm-white front.
front.text: Smooth warm-white stucco wraps the front walls, gables, bay base and corners, under a charcoal standing-seam roof with charcoal fascia; every roof plane is 5 in 12 with 1′0″ eaves, as on the architect's sheets. The entry gable runs on over the covered porch, 1′0″ past the slab, on two stucco piers joined by a tie beam, where a flat porch roof stood before. The window frames are white, with white grid bars dividing the glass of the bay, of the high window over the entrance and of the two sidelights beside the walnut front door. Warm vertical wood cladding lines the recessed entry, and a stained-cedar carriage-house garage door with a top row of glass lites, flanked by black coach lanterns, completes the front. Bedroom 3 keeps its tall bay window and a solid gable above it. The house floor is 11″ above the ground at the front: two equal risers of 5½″, one up to the porch slab and one at the door. The roof follows sheets A1.2, A1.3 and SKA001; the entry roof's height is derived from the site plan, because the set has no elevation of the addition.

B3.label: Bedroom 3
B3.title: A canted bay glazed to the floor.
B3.text: White frames with white grid bars run from the floor to the 7′6″ head, three lites wide and five high in the centre sash and two wide and five high in each side sash, so the bay reads as part of the room and opens it to the front garden. The floor extends into the bay. The bed sits on the west wall, which is solid as on the architect's sheet, under a large canvas. Bay: 8′ wall opening, 2′ projection, glazed to the floor. Above the bay is a continuous plaster gable, and the vaulted ceiling rises from 8′0″ at the side walls to 11′1¼″ at the ridge, lit by a ring pendant. The bathroom's door and the closet's two sliding panels are in the opposite wall, and the 2′8″ door from the foyer is at the side. The foyer wall lines up with the shared bathroom's wall, so the room is 14′11″ wide.

B4.label: Bedroom 4
B4.title: Bedroom 4: a flat ceiling and the bed turned across the room.
B4.text: A calm flat ceiling replaces the vault, at the same 8 ft as the rest of the house. The full bed is turned across the room, with its headboard on the north wall and its side along the window wall, so the room's length stays open from the bed to the door and the reach-in closet. The desk stands in a niche on the north wall, between the nightstand and the back wall of the laundry closet, which takes the room's north-east corner and opens onto the foyer. The west window is 5′0″ wide and centred on its wall, as on the architect's sheet. The room (the architect's office) and its separate reach-in closet keep their positions; overall the room is still 8′0″ deep as on the architect's plan and 14′11″ wide, because its foyer wall lines up with the shared bathroom's wall, and it is now L-shaped around the laundry closet.

K0.label: Kitchen
K0.title: A warm vintage kitchen in cream, oak and brass.
K0.text: Cream shaker cabinets with unlacquered brass cup pulls and knobs, glass-front uppers and a greige tall-cabinet wall at the hall end, where a stainless-steel French-door refrigerator with a bottom freezer drawer stands right beside a built-in microwave over the stainless wall oven. A cream plaster hood with a dentil band rises over a scalloped marble backsplash and a brass pot filler, beside walnut open shelves on whitewashed brick. The fireclay farmhouse sink sits under the white grid window, three sashes of two by four lites in a white casing, with brass sconces and linen café curtains. Amber-glass pendants hang over a white-oak island with a thick grey-veined quartzite top, 7′0″ × 4′0″ as on the architect's sheet, 3′6″ from the sink run and 4′0″ from the cooktop run, with a Persian runner in the work aisle, and a warm oak dining table for six continues the island's west end, toward the hall, under a brass lantern, so the floor between the island and the family room stays open. A 1′10″ × 3′10″ skylight sits on the continuous east roof plane, over the sink and dishwasher. Proposed window: 6′ wide, 3′1¾″ sill, 7′9″ head. Styled after your kitchen style images.

A0.label: Primary bathroom
A0.title: A white primary bath with one wall of stacked stone.
A0.text: The room is white, with one feature wall. Natural stacked stone in warm browns runs the full width and height of the vanity wall, the south wall, behind the floating solid-oak slab with its two basins carved into the wood. Two oak-framed mirrors hang on the stone under a rough dark timber beam, with an enamel-shade lamp over each basin, and a second beam crosses the ceiling. Every other wall is plain white from the floor to the ceiling, above a white tile base and under a white ceiling, and the floor is quiet grey stone. The curbless shower in the north-west corner stands behind frameless glass under the 2′0″ × 2′6″ skylight, lined in matte white tile, with a brushed-nickel rain shower. The room follows the architect's sheet: the toilet is in the south-west corner, the 6′6″ double vanity runs along the south wall, and the door is at the east end of the north wall, off the suite's vestibule and next to the walk-in closet, which is a room of its own behind a sliding pocket door. The west window is 3′0″ wide, from a 2′0″ sill to the ceiling, in a white frame with white grid bars below its transom and a linen roman shade on the sash outside the shower. The stone wall, the oak and the timber follow your primary bathroom wall style image.

A1.label: Shared bathroom
A1.title: A wood-look wall and warm stone in the shared bath.
A1.text: A rustic oak wood-look tile wall rises behind the wall-hung toilet and around a softly lit, wood-lined niche, with warm Spanish-cream stone-look porcelain on the other walls. A floating light-oak vanity carries a honed travertine block with a carved trough basin, a wall-mounted brushed-nickel faucet and a backlit mirror. The floor is light limestone-look tile, and the alcove tub keeps its glass screen and lit niche. The existing tub, vanity, toilet orientation and room footprint remain; the room is entered from the hall through a hinged 2′4″ door. Styled after your shared bathroom style images.

roof.label: Roof connections
roof.title: One roof at 5 in 12, as on the architect's sheets.
roof.text: Every roof plane is 5 in 12, with 1′0″ eaves and a charcoal fascia, as the architect's sheets draw it. The broad main hip has its ridge 14′7″ above the floor. Its east plane runs on over the garage, whose ridge at 12′4½″ ends in the front gable, and its west plane runs on over the bedroom wing to Bedroom 3's front gable. The entry is a raised gable with a level ridge; it runs on over the covered porch, 1′0″ past the slab. Five skylights sit in the roof: over the living room and over the kitchen sink on the east plane, two over the foyer on the entry roof and one over the primary bathroom's shower. The high window over the entrance, 3′ × 2′3″, sits under the entry gable. The roof is shown in charcoal standing-seam metal. The entry roof's height follows from the site plan; framing, loads and drainage detailing remain to be resolved.

LC.label: Laundry closet
LC.title: A stacked washer and dryer off the foyer, next to Bedroom 4.
LC.text: The laundry closet is carved out of Bedroom 4's north-east corner and opens onto the foyer, on its west side right next to the bedroom door. A front-load washer with the dryer stacked on top stands centred behind a pair of narrow doors in a 2′6″ × 6′8″ opening; the doors are hinged on the two jambs and shown wide open against the foyer wall. The closet is 2′10″ wide and 3′0″ deep inside, under the 8 ft ceiling; the oak floor runs in from the foyer, a recessed outlet box and the dryer vent are on the back wall, and a flush light sits in the ceiling. Bedroom 4 keeps its overall size and is L-shaped around the closet. The units are generic models of a typical stacked pair (27″ wide, 30¼″ deep, 39″ high each), not a selected product: connections, vent route and clearances need to be confirmed for the appliances you choose.

changes: Bedroom 4 (plan: office): flat 8 ft ceiling instead of the vault
Front bedroom bay (tour: Bedroom 3, plan: Bedroom #2): glazed down to the floor; window seat removed
Foyer: two skylights on the entry roof's east slope (hall section and vaulted entry)
Primary bedroom: the 7 ft rear window becomes a two-panel sliding door to the garden (landing outside; since the eighth round in the sheet's 6'-4" wall opening)
Bedroom 2 (next to the primary): rear window runs to the ceiling (sill 2'-0" since the third round)

Primary bathroom: tall west window in clear glass, sill 2'-0" since the third round (an evergreen screen in the fenced side yard outside). It stood between the vanity and the shower of the earlier layout; the sixth round moves it to the architect's position and widens it to 3'-0"

Kitchen skylight on the continuous east roof plane over the sink / dishwasher (the concept unit straddled the garage-gable ridge). It was 3'-6" x 4'-0" until the eighth round, which makes it 1'-10" x 3'-10", the size of the outline on the architect's sheet; its east edge stays where it was, 9 1/2 in from the east wall, so the narrower well still lies over the sink
Dining: table in line with the island, no island stools (warm oak under a brass lantern since the third round; moved to the island's west end, 6'-0" x 2'-9" for six, in the fifth round)
Primary bathroom: a 2'-0" x 2'-6" skylight over the shower (in the sixth round it moves with the shower to the room's north-west corner)

The foyer-side wall of Bedroom 4 (office) and Bedroom 3 lines up with the shared bath's east wall: both rooms and the closets between them are 1'-3" wider; foyer and covered porch 5'-9" wide; foyer 18'-6" long as on the plan; the 3'-0" front door stays centred (with a sidelight on each side since the eighth round)

Rear landing outside the living room sized as on the plan, 3'-0" deep (since the eighth round the sheet's 13'-0" x 3'-0" landing, 4 in past each jamb of the living room's sliding door; it ends 1'-1 3/8" short of the east wall's inside face)
Bedroom 2 rear window and the primary bathroom window: a 2'-0" sill instead of glass to the floor (heads stay at the 8 ft ceiling)
Bedroom 4: the bed is turned across the room, headboard on the north wall, so the room's length stays open

Kitchen, primary bathroom, shared bathroom and garage door restyled from the owner's style images (styles/); the primary bathroom's finishes of this round (green shower tile, patterned floor) are superseded by the sixth round, the oak trough vanity stays; the kitchen's black steel grid window and its refrigerator behind cabinet panels are superseded by the seventh round (a white grid window, a visible stainless-steel refrigerator)

Laundry closet with a stacked front-load washer and dryer behind a 2'-6" x 6'-8" door opening. It was first built in the kitchen's south-west corner, where the architect's sheet SKA002 draws "W / D": superseded by the fifth round, which moves it to Bedroom 4
Kitchen south wall re-planned around that closet (closet, refrigerator, wall ovens, a short counter, the cooktop): superseded by the fifth round, the wall is back to its third-round layout

Laundry closet moved out of the kitchen: it is carved out of Bedroom 4's north-east corner and opens east onto the foyer, on the foyer's west side next to the bedroom door. 2'-10" wide x 3'-0" deep clear, the stacked front-load washer and dryer behind a pair of doors in a 2'-6" x 6'-8" opening, shown open

Bedroom 4 is L-shaped after the cut: 14'-11" x 8'-0" overall as before, less 3'-5" x 3'-3" for the closet and its two walls (108.2 sq ft); the desk stands in the niche between the nightstand and the closet's back wall

Dining table moved from the family-room side of the island to the island's west end, the shared-bathroom side, in line with the island: 6'-0" x 2'-9", three chairs on each long side, none at the ends, no rug; the floor between the island and the family room is open

Kitchen south wall back to its third-round layout: refrigerator and oven tower at the west (hall) end, then the counter under three glass-front uppers and the cooktop under the hood (until the seventh round the refrigerator stood behind cabinet panels and the tower held two wall ovens)

Front bedroom suite bathroom (tour: Bedroom 3 bathroom): the window in the shower is vertically larger, from a 3'-0" sill to a 7'-6" head (4'-6" tall; it was 2'-0" tall above a 5'-0" sill). Its 3'-0" width and the obscured glass stay (the frame, black in this round, is white with grid bars since the seventh)

Primary walk-in closet: a small room with a door, as on the last page of sizes.pdf (sheet SKA002). 6'-1" x 8'-0" clear behind a new wall, entered from the suite's vestibule through a sliding pocket door (2'-6" x 6'-8", the leaf slides south into the wall, shown open), with hanging rods and shelves on three sides. The open dressing area with its wardrobes is gone

Primary suite as on the sheet: a vestibule between the closet and the hall, 4'-7" x 8'-0" clear, open to the bedroom over its full width (no door), with the attic access hatch in its ceiling. The suite entry from the hall is a 2'-8" opening with a sliding panel on the hall side, shown open (at the sheet's place since the eighth round, which made Bedroom 2's entry alcove part of the hall; until then it stood beside that alcove, 1'-8" further south)

Primary bedroom as on the sheet: king bed on the west wall, centred between the two west windows, with a nightstand on each side; both west windows are kept (the sheet draws only the north one), and so is the rear sliding door

Primary bathroom laid out as on the sheet: a 5'-0" x 3'-0" curbless shower in the north-west corner, the toilet in the south-west corner, a 6'-6" double vanity along the south wall, the door at the east end of the north wall. The west window is at the sheet's position, 3'-0" wide from the 2'-0" sill to the ceiling, its mullion on the shower's glass line, and the 2'-0" x 2'-6" skylight moved with the shower

Primary bathroom in the style of the owner's image "primary bathroom wall style" (styles/): natural stacked stone on the vanity wall, behind the floating oak vanity with its two wooden troughs and the oak-framed mirrors, under a dark timber beam with enamel lamps; a quiet grey stone floor; brushed nickel fittings. The green shower tile and the blue patterned floor are gone. The grey-green board wainscot with cream plaster above it on the other walls and the cream shower tile of this round are superseded by the seventh round (white walls, white tile)

Refrigerator next to the microwave: the refrigerator stood behind cabinet panels and read as a pantry. It is now a visible stainless-steel French-door refrigerator with a bottom freezer drawer, in the same bay at the hall end of the kitchen's tall wall, under a two-door cabinet. The unit directly beside it, above the wall oven, is a built-in microwave (it was a second wall oven). Nothing else in the kitchen changes

All windows white, with grid lines: every window frame, sash, mullion and transom bar is white, inside and outside, and every window and glazed door has white grid bars (7/8 in wide, on both faces of the glass) with lites as near 14 x 16 1/2 in as each sash allows, the bars in line across sashes and transoms. That includes the primary bedroom's sliding door, the living room's rear glazing and garden door (one four-panel sliding door since the eighth round), the bay, the tall windows of Bedroom 2 and the primary bathroom, the obscured bathroom window, the window above the front door and the kitchen window, which was a black steel grid window and keeps its 2 x 4 lites per sash, now white. The skylights, the shower glass, the garage door and the front door are as they were, shades and curtains stay in front of the grids, and no window opening changes its place or size in this round (the eighth round sets the openings to the architect's sizes and lays their grids out again by the same rule)

Primary bathroom walls coherent and white: the grey-green board wainscot, its cap rail and the cream plaster are removed. Every wall except the vanity wall is plain white from the floor to the ceiling, above a white tile base; the ceiling is white and the shower tile is matte white (it was cream). The stacked stone on the vanity wall stays as the one feature wall, with the timber beams, the oak vanity and mirrors, the lamps, the shelf, the grey stone floor, the fittings and the layout

Fireplace sealed, sofa on that side, television opposite: the living room's fireplace is removed with its stone surround, firebox and hearth ledge, and the east wall is a plain white wall with its baseboard; the east windows are untouched. The sofa stands against that wall, facing west, with a side table and a lamp at each end, a round rug and a round coffee table in front of it and an armchair to the north-west, as the architect's sheet draws it. A 75 in television hangs on the opposite wall, the west wall shared with Bedroom 2, centred on the sofa, over a low oak media console. The way from the dining area to the rear glass and its door stays open

Daylight corrected for the yard, which faces north: the sun was already in the south-east (late morning), but the sky was turned half a circle, with its bright side over the garden. The sky's glow now stands at the sun, over the street side, and its deep-blue side over the garden. The rear of the house, the landings by the house and the near lawn are in the house's shade; no direct sun comes in through the north-facing glass (the primary bedroom's sliding door, Bedroom 2's rear window, the living room's rear glazing), and sun patches fall only through the east windows, the front bay, the window above the front door and the skylights

Exterior: the redesign of the exterior that the owner raised with this round was set aside by the owner. Roof, massing, entry and facade are as they were; only the white window frames and grid bars show outside (the eighth round rebuilds the roof, the porch roof and the ground levels to the architect's sheets; colours and cladding stay)

The model brought to the architect's sheet (sizes.pdf, SKA002) after the size audit: every wall is 5 in thick, inside and outside, and every room stands on the sheet's lines. The house measures 39'-11" x 54'-4" outside (53'-0" on the garage side) and the covered porch is 5'-0" + 2'-4" deep. Your earlier decisions stay: the foyer-side wall of Bedroom 4 and Bedroom 3 on the shared bath's wall line (foyer and porch 5'-9" wide, both rooms 14'-11"), the laundry closet, the second west window of the primary bedroom, the bay glazed to the floor, the kitchen window and the sink under it, the tall windows, the white windows with grid bars, the sealed fireplace, all finishes and furniture

Bedroom 2's corner and the hall as on the sheet: the hall is 3'-3" wide beside a closet block of 7'-8" x 4'-8" and 3'-4" wide south of it. The block holds Bedroom 2's closet (6'-10" wide, two sliding panels in a 6'-0" opening), the furnace closet behind a louvred 1'-8" door and a storage closet behind a 2'-4" door. Bedroom 2 is entered through a hinged 2'-8" door in its south wall (the entry alcove is gone), the shared bathroom has its hinged 2'-4" door, and the primary suite's entry stands at the sheet's place

Kitchen island 7'-0" x 4'-0" at the sheet's place, 3'-6" from the sink run and 4'-0" from the cooktop run; both counters 2'-0" deep. The dining table moved west with the island's end and stays in line with it, with six chairs and 3 ft or more to walk past; the pendants hang over the island's quarter points. The kitchen window, the sink, the refrigerator beside the microwave and the cooktop keep the places you gave them

Bedroom 3's bathroom as on the sheet: a shower 3'-0" wide across the west end, the toilet in a 2'-6" bay and the vanity in a 2'-9" bay on the north wall, a hinged 2'-4" door at the east end of the south wall; the shower window stays as you set it. Bedroom 3's closet is a reach-in closet behind two sliding panels in a 4'-8" opening, and the bedroom's door is 2'-8", hinged on the north side. The window in Bedroom 3's west wall is removed: the sheet has a solid wall behind the bed, where a picture hangs now

Doors and windows at the sheet's sizes and places. Living room rear wall: one 12'-4" four-panel sliding glass door in place of the garden door and the two fixed windows, with its 13'-0" x 3'-0" landing. Primary bedroom: sliding door in a 6'-4" wall opening with a 7'-0" x 3'-0" landing; north west window 3'-0", and your second west window, which keeps its opening, has the same two-sash unit. Bedroom 2 rear window 6'-0". Living room east: one 6'-0" window in place of two; living / dining east window 5'-0". Bedroom 4 west window 5'-0", centred on its wall. Front door 3'-0" with a sidelight on each side, in a unit 5'-3" wide (the sheet's unit fitted to your narrower foyer). Door between house and garage 3'-0", hinged on the north side; a 2'-4" side door in the garage's east wall (2'-8" wall opening); vehicle door in a 15'-0" opening. Every hinged door has a leaf of its opening's size, with hinges and a lever. All new glass is white with grid bars, like the rest

Skylights: the living room gets the sheet's skylight, 1'-10" x 3'-10", where the sheet draws it; the kitchen skylight takes the same size, 1'-10" x 3'-10", and keeps your place over the sink (its east edge where the wider opening's was)

Garage: the floor is 11 in below the house floor, with a step of 1'-0" x 3'-8" at the house door (two risers of 5 1/2 in); the water heater is a 1'-8" tank in the north-east corner (the wall-hung unit is gone)

Roof and levels as on the sheets: every roof plane 5 in 12; main ridge 14'-7" and garage ridge 12'-4 1/2" above the house floor; the entry ridge level; eaves 1'-0" wide. The entry gable runs on over the porch, 1'-0" past the slab, in place of the flat canopy. The house floor is 11 in above the ground at the front and 1'-2" at the rear; the rear landings have one step with two risers of 6 1/2 in, the porch slab is 5 1/2 in below the floor, with two equal risers of 5 1/2 in, one from the front walk up to the slab and one at the door, and the driveway is 18'-1" wide and level. Bedroom 3's vault follows the roof: 8'-0" at the walls, 11'-1 1/4" at the ridge. Colours, cladding and the garage door's design are unchanged

The numbers of the tour follow the rebuilt model: the dimension plan and the schedule are drawn from it, and a door's width in the schedule is its clear opening, the size the architect's sheet gives it
